claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt are single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys.
Equiatomic FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt exhibit soft ferromagnetism with low coercivity.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt have high saturation magnetization.
Partial substitution of Pd or Pt with Al can preserve an almost equiatomic composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Rapid solidification and controlled annealing can promote a high-entropy single-phase structure in the proposed Al-substituted alloy.
Al substitution will induce localized lattice distortions in the FeCoNi-based alloy.
The Al-induced distortion will lower local symmetry and may manifest as partial tetragonal distortion or a mixed microstructure.
Al-induced lattice distortions or associated microstructural features will act as domain-wall pinning sites.
Al has a smaller atomic size than Pd or Pt.
The atomic-size difference between Al and Pd or Pt will create localized lattice strain.
The localized strain will destabilize the high-symmetry fcc lattice.
The strain and symmetry reduction will increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy and pinning will raise the energy barrier for domain-wall motion.
The increased domain-wall-motion barrier will raise the coercive field.
The Al-substituted alloy will have greater coercivity than equivalently processed FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt.
The Al-substituted alloy will largely retain the high saturation magnetization of the baseline.
The coercivity-enhancing effect applies only below the Al content or processing regime that causes significant phase segregation or unwanted secondary phases.
A coercivity increase of more than 10% over an identically processed baseline is the proposed criterion for a successful outcome.

contradictions.description: The conditions call for a single-phase structure without significant secondary phases, whereas the proposed mediator and expected XRD signatures include a mixed microstructure or mixed phases. The hypothesis does not distinguish permissible local heterogeneity from disallowed phase separation.
